claims.claim: Seventy-two small Indian mongooses were released on Hawaiʻi Island in 1883 by sugar planters to control rats in cane fields.
claims.episode_span: Joseph Marsden, later known as “Mongoose Joe,” arranged a larger shipment of seventy-two from Jamaica that same year.
claims.source_title: Did The Mongoose Idea Work? — Images of Old Hawaiʻi
claims.supporting_quote: The next importation was by the Hilo planters, who in 1883 sent Mr. Jonathan Tucker to Jamaica in the West Indies to procure mongoose for them. Mr. Tucker returned with 72 mongoose in good condition, which were liberated in the cane fields in Hilo.

claims.source_title: Mongoose (Urva auropunctata) — Hawaii Invasive Species Council / DLNR
claims.supporting_quote: Mongoose are now widespread on Hawai’i island, Oʻahu, Maui, and Molokai (It is not necessary to report sightings on these islands). There are no known populations on Lanaʻi and Kauaʻi.
